summary.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income grew 7% YoY to INR757 crore and EBITDA rose to INR115 crore at a 15% margin versus 14% a year earlier. Quarterly pre-sales nearly doubled with no new launches, and H1 booking value reached INR1,602 crore (+111% YoY) while collections rose 67% to INR682 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR14 crore-range base as stated; margin 15% vs 14%
Bank interest INR27 crore; government approval-payment interest INR17 crore

segments.name: Thane (owned land)
segments.commentary: 100-acre parcel with INR25,000 crore revenue potential; ~65 acres under development (6.7 mn sq ft RERA carpet, INR16,500 crore potential), INR9,770 crore sold and INR7,977 crore collected to date. Contributed 43% of H1 booking value; Address by GS 1 Tower B (270 units, ~3.5 lakh sq ft) received occupancy certificate.

segments.name: JDA / non-Thane projects
segments.commentary: JDAs are ~52% of GDV with ~INR27,000 crore revenue potential at current prices; four launched JDA projects (Bandra, BKC, Wadala, Sion) have generated INR3,432 crore sales value and INR857 crore collections. Contributed 57% of H1 booking value.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales growth of minimum 20%, reiterated; management says H2 festive season should beat H1 run-rate.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 17-19%; EBITDA growth of about 20% expected for FY27 per management.
No explicit revenue growth guidance this year; management said it should be in the range of about 20%, not significantly different.
FY27 ROCE target 20% and PAT margin 9-10%, maintained.
Interest cost for full year expected at H1 run-rate (no elevation in H2 per management).
Two Mahim launches in H2 (Q3 and Q4 one each) with combined GDV ~INR4,100 crore; one Invictus and one Address product.

Five-year plan: ~20% pre-sales CAGR; BD target of INR8,000-10,000 crore GDV added per year; additional equity of INR400-600 crore may be needed under LRP; debt expected in INR1,200-1,500 crore range and within 1:1 debt-equity.
capex_capacity: Project-level pre-tax cash flow of about INR14,375 crore from current INR52,000 crore GDV; after 5-6% selling costs and ~5% corporate overhead, about INR10,000 crore net pre-tax cash flow over 4-5 years (management estimate).
JDA projects are cash-flow negative for first ~2 years, turning positive from middle of year 3; steady state expected in about 2 years with 8-10 projects outside Thane under execution.
Thane is already net cash positive.

ICICI AIF (10X Realty West subsidiary) invested INR210 crore via OCPRS, ~60% of peak capital need of the Mahim project; company holds 40% capital and receives 5% fee on turnover plus 40% of residual profit.
Promoter equity infusion ~INR400-410 crore; first tranche expected shortly, balance per AGM approval.
Wadala: 1,500 units total, 617 launched (~40%), GDV ~INR5,000 crore with ~45% opened, ~60% of launched units sold.
demand_pricing: Lowest-value Thane apartment is above INR1.5 crore; bulk of MMR inventory is INR3.5-20 crore.
Management views 25-50 bp rate rises as having no major demand impact on its segment; says 75 bp could change decisions at lower price points.
Invictus BKC sales constrained by pending aviation approval for upper floors (expected in weeks); Invictus Thane has limited inventory and Tower A success noted.

Construction costs (labour, cement, steel) rising; ongoing projects are fixed-price contracts with no escalation provision, contingencies held; future launches to be priced to pass on part of cost increases.
Management indicates no intention to build land banks; focus remains MMR JDAs, no plans for other cities currently.

qa_highlights.question: Stake given to ICICI AIF for INR210 crore and why the promoter preferential issue despite earlier no-fundraise stance?
qa_highlights.answer: Structured via OCPRS with economics of 40% capital, 5% turnover fee plus 50% of residual profit; coupon virtually zero and treated as equity. Promoter equity ~INR410 crore cited; management says equity raising was part of the annual plan.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue growth guidance still 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue guidance this year due to percentage-of-completion complexity; management said revenue would be in a similar range to 20%, with EBITDA growth of 20% and pre-sales growth of 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year interest cost exceed the INR100-120 crore range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full-year figure will be in line with H1 run-rate (H1 interest cited at INR91 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Expected debt trajectory and use of promoter money?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt will not fall for 1-2 years; expected to stay in INR1,200-1,500 crore range within 1:1 D/E. ICICI OCPRS will not be classed as debt; receipt of entire ICICI sum by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Pre-sales guidance implies ~INR2,000 crore in H2; how much from existing portfolio and Mahim product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said existing-portfolio pre-sales would be much more than INR1,000 crore; Mahim will have one Invictus and one Address tower; towers will not mix product types.

qa_highlights.question: Is weakness in luxury/ultra-luxury (Invictus Thane, BKC) structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Thane is a test market, limited Invictus inventory introduced; BKC upper-floor sales await aviation approval and RERA registration in the coming weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term pre-sales CAGR and capital needs?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% pre-sales CAGR over next 5 years under the new LRP; additional equity of INR500-600 crore (later INR400-600 crore) may be needed; BD target INR8,000-10,000 crore GDV per year.

qa_highlights.question: How are construction cost increases being managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Ongoing projects are fixed-price with no escalation; contingencies absorb fluctuations. Future launches to be priced to pass on part of cost increases, with margin expected to be maintained if inflation is temporary.

risks_watch: Rising construction costs (labour, cement, steel) for future launches under fixed-price contracts with limited escalation.
Debt staying at INR1,200-1,500 crore and interest cost run-rate (H1 INR91 crore); cash flow negative in early JDA years.
BKC Invictus upper-floor sales dependent on pending aviation approval and RERA registration.
Revenue guidance withdrawn for FY27; percentage-of-completion makes turnover less predictable.
Stock valuation roughly 50% below listing levels; institutional coverage limited (one analyst) and index exclusion cited.
Mahim launches (INR4,100 crore GDV) in Q3 and Q4 FY27; inventory opened at launch not yet decided.
Interest-rate sensitivity if rates rise 50-75 bp; management's view that demand is resilient is its own assessment.
summary.management_tone: Confident and assertive on execution, pre-sales momentum and the ICICI structure, with direct answers on debt and cost. More guarded on revenue guidance (explicitly withheld) and on near-term cost inflation, which it described as a concern for the industry.
key_quotes: We achieved a landmark milestone this quarter by nearly doubling our quarterly pre -sales without any new launches, driven entirely by robust sales velocity and steady price realizations within our existing product portfolio.

So, as a result of that, we remain firmly on track to achieve our full -year guidance of 20% minimum pre-sales growth, return on capital employed of 20% and our EBITDA margins for the year will range between 17% to 19% and the PAT margin will be 9% to 10%.
But on the ongoing project, there is no immediate impact that we have today.

It will not come down at least for the next 1 or 2 years for sure, because we are continuing to grow and we are adding new projects and we want to grow and we don't want to raise any kind of significant equity going forward.

adds.what: Two Mahim launches (one Invictus, one Address) with combined GDV ~INR4,100 crore; these are project launches, not owned productive capacity

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 pre-sales growth of at least 20% and EBITDA growth of about 20%, and said revenue growth should be around 20% after formally dropping revenue guidance; backing is partial, with H2 Mahim launches (~INR4,100 crore GDV) and H1 booking value up 111% but no capacity additions.
